title: Run Megahit using iMicrobe
author: Alise J Ponsero
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.uk5euy6

steps.title: Launch Megahit App
steps.instruction: Access the Megahit assembly tool via the iMicrobe platform.

steps.title: Provide Input Data
steps.instruction: Input the sequencing reads using a Cyverse datastore or URL (cart input is not supported).

substeps.instruction: For paired-end reads: Open the datastore and provide the forward read and reverse read files in the corresponding input fields.
For single-end reads: Open the datastore and provide the reads in the 'single-end reads' input field.

steps.title: Configure Assembly Parameters
steps.instruction: Optionally tune assembly parameters by entering arguments in the 'Additional Command Line Arguments' field.

substeps.instruction: Set k-mer strategy using --k-min (minimum k), --k-max (maximum k), and --k-step (iteration step); k must be odd and step must be even.
Set --min-count to discard (k min +1)-mers with multiplicity lower than d (default is 2; use 3 for high sequencing depth coverage >40x).
Use --no-mercy for generic datasets >= 30x to potentially generate better results.
Use --kmin-1pass to activate K-min-1 pass mode for ultra low-depth datasets to improve memory efficiency.

steps.title: Retrieve and Analyze Results
steps.instruction: Access the output files from the CyVerse datastore after the job has run.

substeps.instruction: Select the corresponding run and go to the 'Outputs' section.
Click 'Browse and view output files in the CyVerse Datastore'.
Navigate to the 'megahit-out' folder to find the following files:
log and opts.txt: Running log and chosen parameters.

intermediate_contigs folder: Contains k K .contigs.fa (de Bruijn graph order-K), k K .addi.fa (after removing local low coverage unitigs), k K .local.fa (locally assembled contigs for k=K), and k K .final.contigs.fa (stand-alone contigs for k=K).
